content:
We need a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: step1: amide formation (carboxylic acid to amide). So forward: acid + amine -> amide. Retrosynthetic: break amide bond to give carboxylic acid and amine.

Step2: Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (the double bond). So forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> unsaturated acid. Retrosynthetic: break C=C double bond to give aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually the product is α,β-unsaturated acid attached to aromatic ring. So we can disconnect the double bond to give aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid.

Step3: Sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So retrosynthetic: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride and amine.

Thus overall: target has sulfonamide linking an aniline (aryl amine) to sulfonyl group attached to another phenyl ring bearing the unsaturated amide side chain.

So propose disconnections:

1) Break amide C(=O)-NH linking the unsaturated side chain to aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So precursors: aromatic aldehyde (c3ccccc3)?? Wait the amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). The amide carbonyl is attached to the unsaturated chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-aryl. So the amide carbonyl is attached to the unsaturated chain (alpha,beta unsaturated acid). So retrosynthesis: break amide to give carboxylic acid (the unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The amine is an aniline with an NH2 (para? Actually Nc3ccccc3N indicates an aniline with an NH attached to carbonyl and also an NH2? Wait the SMILES: ...C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. That is an amide where the nitrogen is attached to phenyl ring which also has an NH2 substituent (an aniline). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl ring (anilide) and the phenyl also has an NH2 (para? not important). So the amine precursor is 4-aminophenyl? Actually the SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with an extra N? Let's parse: c3ccccc3 is phenyl; preceding N is attached to carbonyl: C(=O)N- phenyl; after phenyl there is N (attached to phenyl). So it's an aniline with an amino substituent at some position (maybe para). So the amine precursor is 4-aminophenylamine? Actually it's 1,4-diaminobenzene (p-phenylenediamine). So the amide formation uses p-phenylenediamine (or aniline with NH2). So step1: amide formation between unsaturated acid and p-phenylenediamine (one amine used). The other amine remains free for later sulfonamide formation.

2) The unsaturated acid precursor can be obtained via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (maybe 4-methylbenzaldehyde? Actually the aromatic ring attached to the unsaturated chain is the same phenyl as the amide? Wait the unsaturated chain attaches to the phenyl ring that also has the amine. The unsaturated chain is attached to the phenyl via the carbonyl (amide). The double bond is conjugated to the phenyl ring? The SMILES: /C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N. The double bond is attached to the carbonyl carbon? Actually /C=C/C(=O)N- phenyl. So the double bond is attached to carbonyl carbon via the carbonyl carbon? The pattern: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph. So the unsaturated acid is trans-3-phenylacrylic acid? Wait unsaturated acid: C=C-COOH? The Doebner modification yields α,β-unsaturated acid attached to aromatic aldehyde. So the aldehyde would be the phenyl ring (c3ccccc3) with an aldehyde substituent (maybe at position where the chain attaches). So the aldehyde is 4-aminobenzaldehyde? Actually the phenyl has an NH2 substituent elsewhere. So the aldehyde precursor is 4-aminobenzaldehyde (p-aminobenzaldehyde). Then Doebner with malonic acid gives p-aminocinnamic acid (trans-4-aminocinnamic acid). Then amide formation with p-phenylenediamine? Wait p-aminocinnamic acid has an NH2 on the phenyl, and the acid group is at the end of the chain. Then coupling with another aniline? Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring (the same ring). In p-aminocinnamic acid, the acid is at the side chain, the amine is on the ring. To form amide, we need an amine (maybe aniline) to react with the acid. But the target amide nitrogen is attached to the same phenyl ring (intramolecular?). Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring (the same ring) and also attached to carbonyl. So the amide is formed between the acid (cinnamic acid) and the aniline (same ring). That would be intramolecular cyclization? But the target shows N attached to phenyl and also carbonyl attached to chain; the phenyl also has another NH2 (maybe at para). So the amide nitrogen is part of the same phenyl ring (i.e., anilide). So the amide formation could be between p-aminocinnamic acid and aniline (same molecule) but that would be intramolecular; but the guidance says each step is forward reaction; we can treat as intermolecular: use p-aminocinnamic acid (acid) and aniline (amine) to form amide, then later sulfonamide attaches to the other amine (the aniline's other NH2). However the product would have two phenyl rings? Wait the target has two phenyl rings: one is the sulfonyl phenyl (c2ccc...), the other is the aniline phenyl (c3ccccc3N). So the amide nitrogen is attached to the aniline phenyl (c3...). So the amide formation uses that phenyl as amine, and the acid is the unsaturated acid attached to the sulfonyl phenyl? Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to the sulfonyl phenyl? Let's parse full SMILES:

Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have a tolyl (C- methyl) phenyl (ring1) attached to sulfonamide: NS(=O)(=O) attached to second phenyl (ring2). On ring2, there is a substituent /C=C/C(=O)N- phenyl (ring3) with NH2. So ring2 is sulfonyl phenyl; ring3 is aniline with NH2; the unsaturated chain connects ring2 to amide carbonyl to ring3.

Thus step breakdown:

- Step3 (forward): sulfonamide formation: sulfonyl chloride (SO2Cl) reacting with aniline (ring1) to give sulfonamide linking ring1 to sulfonyl phenyl (ring2). In retrosynthesis, break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride attached to ring2 and aniline (ring1). So precursors: p-toluidine (or methyl phenyl amine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from ring2 (maybe 4-(cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride). Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to ring2 which also bears the unsaturated chain. So we need sulfonyl chloride: ClSO2-aryl (ring2 with unsaturated chain). So step3: target -> sulfonyl chloride + aniline (ring1). Good.

- Step2 (forward): Doebner modification to create the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to ring2 (aryl). So retrosynthesis: break the double bond to give aromatic aldehyde (ring2 with aldehyde) and malonic acid. So precursor: aldehyde (aryl-CHO) where the aldehyde is on ring2 at the position where the chain attaches (para to sulfonyl?). The aldehyde also has the sulfonyl chloride attached (since we haven't yet formed sulfonamide). So we need aldehyde with sulfonyl chloride substituent.

- Step1 (forward): amide formation between the unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) and aniline (ring3) to give amide. Retrosynthesis: break amide to give unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) and aniline (ring3). The unsaturated acid is the product of Doebner step (cinnamic acid attached to ring2). So step1: unsaturated acid + aniline (p-phenylenediamine? Actually the amine is aniline with NH2 substituent). The amine is 4-aminophenyl (ring3). So we need that amine.

Thus overall route:

Target -> (retro step3) sulfonyl chloride (aryl with aldehyde side chain) + p-toluidine (methyl phenyl amine). Then sulfonyl chloride precursor still has aldehyde side chain.

Next retro step2: sulfonyl chloride aldehyde -> sulfonyl chloride + aromatic aldehyde? Wait we already have aldehyde as part of sulfonyl chloride. Actually step2 is Doebner: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So retro: unsaturated acid (attached to sulfonyl chloride) -> aldehyde (aryl-CHO with sulfonyl chloride) + malonic acid. So we need aldehyde with sulfonyl chloride substituent.

Thus after step2, we have aldehyde (aryl-CHO with sulfonyl chloride) and malonic acid (simple). Then step1: amide formation between unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) and aniline (p-phenylenediamine). But unsaturated acid is produced from step2, not directly from aldehyde. So we need to combine steps: after step2 we have unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) attached to sulfonyl chloride phenyl. Then step1 uses that unsaturated acid + aniline (p-phenylenediamine) to give amide. So the route is:

1) Amide formation: cinnamic acid (aryl-CH=CH-COOH) + 4-aminophenylamine (p-phenylenediamine) -> amide (cinnamoyl amide attached to phenyl with NH2). This yields intermediate: aryl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph(NH2). (This is the part of target without sulfonamide.)

2) Doebner modification: aldehyde (aryl-CHO) + malonic acid -> cinnamic acid (aryl-CH=CH-COOH). The aldehyde is the same aryl as in step1 (the sulfonyl phenyl). So we need aldehyde with sulfonyl chloride substituent? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the same aryl ring (ring2). In target, the sulfonyl group is attached to ring2, and the unsaturated chain is also attached to ring2 (para). So the aldehyde precursor must have both substituents: sulfonyl chloride at one position, aldehyde at para position. So aldehyde: 4-(chlorosulfonyl)benzaldehyde (or 4-sulfonyl chloride benzaldehyde). So step2: 4-(chlorosulfonyl)benzaldehyde + malonic acid -> 4-(chlorosulfonyl)cinnamic acid.

3) Sulfonamide formation: 4-(chlorosulfonyl)cinnamic acid amide intermediate + p-toluidine (methyl phenyl amine) -> target sulfonamide.

Thus we need to find templates for each step.

We have template for amide formation (functional groups broken: carboxylic acid; formed: amide). The search gave template ID 401931 (retro_smarts). That template seems to convert amide to acid + amine? The retro_smarts: '[#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])/[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]>>C-C(-C)(-C)-O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[#7:2])=[O;D1;H0:3].O-C(=O)-[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]'

So that is a retro template that breaks amide to give acid and amine plus a tert-butyl protecting group? Not sure. But we can use it.

We also need Doebner modification template: functional groups broken: aldehyde, carboxylic acid? Actually forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> unsaturated acid. So retro: break C=C double bond, form aldehyde and malonic acid. So functional groups broken: C-C double bond (maybe). Formed: aldehyde, carboxylic acid. Let's search.
